summary: ```# Introduction to New Features in Marvelous Designer 2025.0 - Module Library Updates Welcome to the new feature introduction video of Marvelous Designer 2025. In this version, you can experience the latest module library designed to improve your work efficiency. ## Module Library Overview In the window options in the main menu, you can choose to display or hide the module library window. The module editor and previous module editor have been integrated into the module library. As in the previous version, click the small arrow in the upper right corner to choose whether to fold or display the module library window. In the earlier version, the module components were defined in the module editor. Now, you can directly define the module components in the module library. The structure order of the module library is organized by group type and style component. This current structure order is very convenient for the management and integration of design components. If you need to define certain versions of the 3D window as components, you must follow the structure from the group to find the corresponding style type. ## Module Library Structure Now we will explain the module library structure from the outside to the inside. - The **outer layer** is the group. You can choose a group to add styles or click the add button in the upper right corner to select the group to add. - Choose the folder to store the group files, and the categories and styles of the subordinates will be stored in this folder. - Click the right arrow on the group file folder to copy the file folder path or delete the file folder. You can click the refresh button to refresh the group list. In this tutorial, we will choose the male group. When you double-click a group, it will display the categories below the group. In the upper left corner, you can see the structure of the current folder. Click the group name to return to the group list. ## Adding Categories and Styles You can use the existing category or click the add button to add a category. For example, adding a clothing category. Click the refresh button to refresh the category folder. However, only the folder that contains the component module will be displayed in the module library. In the category folder, click the right arrow to copy the folder path or delete the file folder. In this tutorial, we will choose the Basic Shirts category. When you double-click the category folder, it will display all the categories below it. ## Defining Styles Now, we will add the original half-sleeved T-shirt from the default asset library as an example to define the style. Click the add button in the upper right corner and choose the add style menu. In the pop-up window, enter the name and set the shortcut. The app will default to use the fashion shortcut in the 3D window. If you want to use other pictures as shortcuts, you can click the icon on the camera and then go to the folder. You can click the icon mode to switch the display mode to preview or list type. Click the refresh button to refresh the style list. Click the right arrow on the style shortcut and select the edit style menu. You can adjust the style shortcut or name. You can also delete the style type by removing the options. ## Assigning Styles to Product Lines Click the add button in the upper right corner to assign the style to the product line. After selecting this option, you will add a new product line file to the top of the style under the category. You can expand these styles. In the top right corner of the product line list, click the add product line option. In the pop-up window, set the name and shortcut of the new product line. You can also add a new product line to the same style and then copy the selected product line. Double-click to open the product line. You can see the style type below. First, select a clothing type, then select a style type. For example, choose a men's top and the low-brow embroidery style. After opening, you can see the component modules of each part under the selected style. ## Managing Components Double-click on other styles to switch under the same type. You will see the components of the front, back, sleeves, and collar here. Each type of component has multiple components to change. This is similar to the previous modular configuration. The double-click module component will be added to the component. If there is a component, it will switch to the selected component. Each part of the clothing is called a component. For example, in a T-shirt, the components are the front, back, sleeves, and collar. After setting the component type, you can define the clothing version in the 3D window and designate it as a variety of components. ## Adding New Component Types Now let's learn how to add a component type without a component structure. Click on the add button in the upper right corner to open the add menu. Select Add Component Type. You can set the new component type in the pop-up window. The top type is the clothing location of the component, and the bottom is the type label to set them. In the default situation, the label and the selected component type are the same. However, you can modify it according to your needs. If you want to create different styles or types of design for the same part, you can use the labels as classification. You can choose to save the component configuration in the upper right corner. After saving, these component types will be stored as configuration files. The next time you open it, you can call this component structure by selecting the open component configuration option. ## Using Automatic Module Fastening Later, we will learn how to use the automatic module fastening label function. Click on the add button in the upper right corner to open the new component list. When all component types are set, you can start adding components for each type. Click on the add new component button in the upper right corner of the component type. The module generator window will appear, displaying a list of module types. Here you can manage the components under each type. In the upper right corner, you can choose to edit the module type and configuration. In the module edit area, you can save, edit, or delete these module components. Using the automatic module fastening label option, you can quickly separate the modules into each component type. After selecting the option, you will see that each module automatically changes its color to distinguish its component type. You can refer to the name and color to determine whether these modules are correctly matched to the type of component. ## Saving Modules and Confirming Selections If the modules are correctly matched to the component type, click on the save button on the right side of the camera icon to save the module. When the module is correctly saved, the hook icon on the left side will light up, indicating that the module has been activated. If the automatic module fastening function is not working correctly, you can click on the marker icon to manually select the module type. You can click on the module type or hold the shift key to select multiple modules, then press the enter key to confirm the selection. When all the module types are correctly saved, the add button on the bottom will activate. After clicking on the add button, a spring will pop up. Click on the prompt operation to check whether the sewing line structure between the modules is correct. Click on the sewing line to see the marking on the sewing line. The prompt will show the label of the module component on both sides of the sewing line. If the sewing line is incorrect, please click on the cancel button to manually adjust the sewing line and try again. ## Finalizing Module Definitions After confirming the sewing line, click on the confirm key to finalize the definition of the module. Then adjust the clothing panel and re-register an additional module. Click on the add new module button in the upper right corner of the module type. The window of the 2D panel will switch to selecting panels. Follow the mouse button to select the panels in the 2D window. Click on the shift key to select multiple panels, and then press the enter key to confirm the selection of panels. Edit the shrink chart and name. As the new modules increase, you can switch them in the module library. After switching the modules, the system will automatically detect the matching between the modules and return the sewing line. ## Module Management Options Click the right button on the module to select the corresponding option in the menu. You can delete the selected module, share the selected module with other models under the same category, change the shrink chart, or replace the shrink chart of the module with a new one. Finally, let's look at the related settings of the module in the user's self-definition. Go to the main menu, select user self-definition, and find other options. ### Module Protection Settings Protect module optimization by limiting editing. When this option is selected, add, edit, delete, and automatic module optimization labels will no longer be usable. You can reduce the number of modules and limit editing, prohibiting a mixture of modules of different styles. After opening the module, you can’t mix different modules to create one set of clothing. When you add a module from a different style, a warning window will pop up. If necessary, you can click the window button to select and verify. Thank you for watching this tutorial on the new features in Marvelous Designer 2025.0! ```
